race_context: The district: Norwell Community Schools (formerly Northern Wells Community Schools), based in Ossian, serves northern Wells County through four schools: Norwell High School, Norwell Middle School, Lancaster Elementary and Ossian Elementary {nwcs_home}{nces_nwcs}. Federal data list 2,413 students in the 2024-25 school year; the district's 2027 budget presentation estimates its state-funded enrollment (ADM) at 2,294, down from 2,414 in 2023 {nces_nwcs}{nwcs_budget_2027}. Mike Springer is superintendent {nwcs_agenda_0922}.

The board has five members: Chad Kline, Traci Neuenschwander, Corey Krug, Cathie Peterson and Todd Nash {nwcs_members}{nwcs_bid_notice}. County results show one seat each for Jefferson, Lancaster, Rockcreek and Union townships plus one at-large seat; the Jefferson and Lancaster seats were on the 2024 ballot (won by Nash and Peterson) and the at-large, Rockcreek and Union seats on the 2022 ballot {wc_2024_results}{wc_2022_results}. Each township race appears on ballots across the district, so all district voters vote in every race {wc_ballot_union}{wc_ballot_rockcreek}.
Seats on the 2026 ballot: three seats, one each for At Large, Rockcreek Township and Union Township, each 'Vote For One (1) Only,' matching the state list {wc_ballot_union}{in_list}.

At Large: Corey Krug won this seat unopposed in 2018 and 2022 and is not on the 2026 ballot {wc_2018_results}{wc_2022_results}{wc_candidates}. The News-Banner reported that Deborah Adams withdrew from the at-large race, leaving Angie Topp and Steve Garza in a contest; it described the race as an open seat with a former board member and a newcomer running {nb_ballot_final}{nb_garza_topp}.
Rockcreek Township: Chad Kline, the board president, won the seat unopposed in 2022 and is running unopposed {wc_2022_results}{nb_kline_seal}{wc_candidates}.

Union Township: Traci Neuenschwander won the seat unopposed in 2022 and is not on the 2026 ballot; Jessica Bender is the only candidate, so the seat will change hands {wc_2022_results}{wc_candidates}.

Party labels: under Indiana's new law allowing school board candidates to list a party, Angela K Topp and Steve Garza are listed as Republicans; Chad L Kline and Jessica Bender did not list a party {wc_candidates}{in_list}.

Budget and the 2025 property-tax law (September 2026): at its Sept. 22, 2026 budget hearing the district estimated an annual Operations Fund revenue loss of about $590,000, not counting a possible $450,000 loss in local income tax revenue, and proposed a 2027 tax rate of $0.9607 per $100 of assessed value, up from $0.8934 in 2026; its example showed a $250,000 home's school tax bill falling slightly (from $983 to $958) because of larger deductions under Senate Enrolled Act 1 {nwcs_budget_2027}. The News-Banner reported the district was seeking a higher tax rate in anticipation of lower revenue from state tax changes {nb_tax_rate}. The 2027 Education Fund budget is $18.4 million and the Operations Fund about $9 million; the board was scheduled to adopt the budget Oct. 13, 2026 {nwcs_budget_2027}{nwcs_agenda_0922}.

Staffing (May 2026): Springer's May 12, 2026 report listed 2026-27 reductions of nine non-special-needs teaching assistant positions, 2.79 certified teaching positions, a technology integration specialist and a business office position, while keeping elementary class sizes low and the middle school teaming model {nwcs_supt_0512}. A News-Banner headline reported the district would reduce 14 staff in 2026-27 {nb_staff_cuts}.

Teacher pay (August 2026): at its collective bargaining hearing the district reported starting teacher pay rose from $37,208 to $46,920 since 2020 and estimated a 3% raise would cost about $450,960 {nwcs_budget_2027}{nb_salary}.

Bonds and facilities (2025–2026): in September 2025 the board considered a general obligation bond of up to $2.5 million instead of the $7.9 million discussed earlier, and a $1.65 million bond was approved in October 2025 {nb_bond_2025}{nb_bond_165}. The 2027 capital projects plan totals $2,279,000, led by a $1.1 million roof replacement at the high school and middle school {nwcs_budget_2027}. New inclusive playgrounds opened at the elementary schools in August 2026 {nb_playgrounds}.

Homeschool access to extracurriculars (2026): Springer proposed lowering the number of classes homeschool students must take to join extracurricular activities from five to two; the board instead voted 4–1 in April 2026 to set the minimum at four classes starting in 2026-27 {nb_homeschool_proposal}{nb_homeschool_vote}.

Safety (2026): in June 2026 the district moved to add a special deputy, a former Indiana State Police officer, to its staff in partnership with the Wells County sheriff, and the district reported two certified school resource officers on campus {nb_special_deputy}{nwcs_budget_2027}.

Other 2026 actions: the board revised preschool programming after state reductions to On My Way Pre-K vouchers, drafted a wireless device policy for the state cell phone law, and adopted new booster-club guidelines in September 2026 {nwcs_agenda_0113}{nwcs_supt_0512}{nb_booster}. In May 2026 the board reviewed buying AI accounts-payable software, with an in-house option estimated at up to $30,000 in the first year {nwcs_supt_0512}.
Forums: the News-Banner announced a candidate forum for some contested Wells County races in early October 2026; whether Norwell candidates took part could not be confirmed {nb_forum_notice}.
